stem.text: When a small sample of hydrocarbon Q is completely combusted, it produces $3.52\,\text{g}$ of carbon dioxide and $1.44\,\text{g}$ of water.
What could be the structure of hydrocarbon Q?

A.alt: Skeletal formula of a six-membered ring with three C=C double bonds (Kekule benzene)

B.alt: Skeletal formula of an eight-membered carbon ring with no double bonds (cyclooctane)

C.alt: Formula H–C≡C–C≡C–H printed on one line, with triple bonds

D.alt: Skeletal formula of a six-membered ring with one C=C double bond (cyclohexene)
